subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` knob now, and must this PR preserve shipped no-override `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior for subagent and cron sessions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this PR adds a public config/default surface and changes existing hook-extra context behavior in a way that can alter upgraded users' agent sessions.

options.title: Preserve shipped defaults, then review the tier knob
options.body: Keep no-override `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior unchanged, apply hook-source exclusion only to explicit tier modes, add docs/tests, then let maintainers decide whether the additive config surface should land.

options.title: Accept the breaking no-override guard
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally make subagent/cron defaults root-only, but the PR should then include explicit upgrade documentation and compatibility proof for affected hook users.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap selection
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve tiering with the broader context/bootstrap selection proposals so OpenClaw gets one long-term public contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve shipped defaults, then review the tier knob
recommendation.body: Keep no-override `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior unchanged, apply hook-source exclusion only to explicit tier modes, add docs/tests, then let maintainers decide whether the additive config surface should land.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest feature-history signal for subagent bootstrap limiting and prior review context on the paired issue.
